Ms. Anjali Bansal
Because good counselling starts with listening.
Meet your counsellor

Counselling that starts with a conversation, not a checklist.

Through her experience with some of India's renowned IB schools, Ms. Bansal has counselled thousands of students, each with their own personality, strengths and dreams. For her, counselling has never been about marks in, universities out.

What does the student enjoy?
What are they good at?
What matters to the family?

There is no single "best university." There is only the right fit for the student.

"There is no perfect university for everyone. The right choice depends on the student."

I don't believe counselling should begin with "Which university do you want to apply to?" It should begin with "Tell me about yourself."

If we think an option is a great fit, we'll tell you. If there's a better one, we'll tell you that too, and if something doesn't look realistic, we'll be honest rather than make a promise we can't keep.

Anjali Bansal
Founder & Lead Education Counsellor
Our approach

We look at the student sitting in front of us.

We start with the student

Only after we understand who a student is do we start talking about countries and universities.

We talk about real costs

Tuition, accommodation, visas, flights, insurance. Families shouldn't discover the true cost after deciding.

We don't chase university names

A famous university can be wonderful, but it isn't automatically right. Sometimes another fits better.

Destinations

Where can your journey take you?

Depending on course, profile, budget and goals, other destinations may also be considered.

From "I don't know" to "I know what to do"

Your journey with us, step by step.

01

Our first conversation

No complicated forms, no pressure. We learn about the student, their goals and what the family has in mind.

02

Understanding the profile

Academics, English qualifications, interests, career aspirations and budget, to understand, not judge.

03

Exploring countries

We compare countries on what matters to the student, and explain advantages and limitations clearly.

04

Finding the course

The best application won't help if the student doesn't enjoy the course once they get there.

05

Building a university list

A sensible mix of ambitious, good-fit and alternative options, not everywhere, just the right places.

06

Applications

Forms, portals, SOPs, LORs and offer letters, with everything submitted kept genuine and accurate.

07

Scholarships

We can't promise a scholarship, but we make sure students know what's available and how to approach it.

08

Financial planning

The goal isn't simply to get a student abroad. It's making sure the family is comfortable with the decision.

09

Visa preparation

We do not guarantee visas. No honest counsellor can control a government decision.

10

Getting ready to leave home

Pre-departure guidance on banking, health, accommodation and travel before departure.

Frequently asked

Questions families often ask.

My grades aren't very high. Can I still study abroad?

+

Possibly. There are many universities with different entry requirements. We look at your complete profile and discuss realistic options.

I don't know what I want to study.

+

That's okay. Many students don't. Counselling can help you explore your interests and possible directions before you decide.

Can my parents join the counselling?

+

Of course, we actually encourage it, particularly when discussing finances and major decisions.

Will you guarantee my visa?

+

No, and we think you should be cautious of anyone who does. We help you prepare carefully, but the final decision belongs to the government authority.

What if I have a study gap?

+

A study gap does not automatically prevent you from studying abroad. Circumstances, destination and requirements all matter.

Can you help me after I arrive?

+

Post-arrival guidance is included in selected packages.
